html:
The Pokanoket were the leading band of the Wampanoag people, with their main village at Sowams near Mount Hope, in today's Bristol, Rhode Island. Their sachem Massasoit was the chief sachem of the Wampanoag when the English arrived.

Epidemics in the years before 1620 had killed many of his people, while their rivals the Narragansett were spared. In 1621 Massasoit made an alliance with the new English settlers of Plymouth Colony, partly to balance the Narragansett. The alliance held for some forty years.

As English settlement spread, the peace broke down. Massasoit's son Metacom, called King Philip by the English, led King Philip's War in 1675 and 1676, one of the deadliest wars in colonial America for its size. Metacom was killed near Mount Hope in 1676, and many Wampanoag were killed or sold into slavery. A Pokanoket group still exists in Rhode Island.
